checklist.evidence: Diagnoses blame Deployment/vigil-app and upstream app-backend, not the ground-truth fault origin vigil-worker-1.
The diagnosis identifies downstream application readiness failures as root causes instead of the worker-node sysctl fault.
It misidentifies vigil-app and app-backend as fault origins; neither is the specified vigil-worker-1 component.
It describes resource sizing, probe timeouts, and upstream failure rather than runtime sysctl drift.
It omits net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables, its incorrect value 0, restore value 1, and target host.
The attributed memory, probe, and upstream faults are unrelated to the injected sysctl networking mutation.
It blames vigil-app configuration, stress-ng, nginx, and app-backend, none identified as contributing in ground truth.
The required affected component vigil-worker-1 is never mentioned in either diagnosis.
Readiness deadline and upstream timeout symptoms are described, not pod networking breakage from disabled bridge iptables.

diagnosis_text:
Diagnosis 1:
 root_cause: The declared vigil-app pod spec under-sizes the nginx container (memory limit 128Mi) while co-scheduling a memory-hogging stress-ng sidecar (--vm-bytes 50M within a 96Mi limit) and sets readinessProbe timeoutSeconds=1, shorter than nginx's 2s proxy_connect/read timeouts for /healthz, so nginx worker stalls cause every readiness probe to hit "context deadline exceeded" and the Deployment never reports an available replica. root_cause_component: Deployment/vigil-app
 recommended_action: git_commit_k8s

Diagnosis 2:
 root_cause: The vigil-app readiness probe path /healthz is a pure reverse proxy to REQUIRED_API_BASE (http://app-backend), so pod readiness is entirely dependent on the upstream app-backend endpoint; app-backend stopped serving requests, and nginx's readiness proxy connection times out, leaving both vigil-app replicas at 1/2 Ready. root_cause_component: Deployment/vigil-app (container vigil-app, upstream Service/app-backend 10.250.87.68:80)
 recommended_action: escalate
